content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am a student working on a project for a tractor pull club and am new to [product_name]. I'm trying to connect and program a ground speed sensor using [product_name]. The sensor uses a connector with four pins: ground, enable, 12 volt, and signal. Can anyone help me get started? I've watched online tutorials. We also plan to connect a proximity switch to measure wheel speed, with the goal of calculating wheel slip ratio. Is this possible with the [product_name] programming software? Thanks for any advice!
Could you specify the sensor's manufacturer and model or order number? Even better, please provide a datasheet.

The sensor link doesn't provide detailed information about its signal. It requires 12VDC power, which isn't an issue for [product_name], but we on the forum aren't sure about the nature of the output signal. Is it 0-12V, 12-0V, PWM, frequency, or a bus signal like CAN-bus? You need to clarify the signal type so we can assist you further.
I have additional information now. I've attached the user guide. Starting from page 8: [url] Also, starting on page 17: [url]

It appears your sensor has a pulse output with an open collector. To use it with [product_name], a pull-up resistor is needed. According to the manual (.pdf), a 10 kOhm resistor is required—place it between the power supply positive and the digital input of [product_name]. Your sensor outputs roughly 128 pulses for every meter moved, which you should count. Note: Most inputs on [product_name] are slow, handling up to 4 pulses per second, while fast inputs (not available on all [product_name] models) can manage up to 5000 pulses per second.

Does resistor power rating matter here? I've only used standard resistors for breadboards before—is that suitable? Should I just splice it into the circuit? I also found this note in the manual: 'Do not connect an external power supply in parallel to the output load of a DC output, as this could create a reverse current unless a diode or similar protective device is installed.' Thanks for your much-needed assistance!

No, the required power rating for the resistor is very low—0.25 or 0.5 watt is sufficient. The resistance value should be between 1 kOhm and 10 kOhm; any value in this range will work, it's not critical.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants need help integrating third-party sensors with [product_name], particularly with adapting pulse outputs and understanding input limitations. Incomplete documentation and the lack of targeted tutorials for hardware connections pose challenges, especially for newcomers.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect clear, simple guidance for connecting pulse-output speed sensors to [product_name], configuring sensors through the appropriate software, and performing calculations like slip ratio. They want an uncomplicated setup process that covers hardware connections and programming basics.
